I got tired of ad-heavy JSON formatters so I built my own — here's what I learned
entry.summary: I use JSON formatters every day. Paste messy API response, get clean output. Simple. getpdfmint.com/tools/json-formatter Auto-fix Schema fix This one is for when your JSON is technically valid but the types are wrong. Classic example: your API returns {"port": "8080", "retries": "3"} - valid JSON, but both values should be numbers, not strings. Schema fix detects string-wrapped numbers and booleans and converts them to their proper types automatically. It's a small thing but it saves a surprising amount of time when you're debugging why your config isn't being read correctly. What I learned building it Syntax highlighting without a library is surprisingly doable with a regex pass over the output. The hard part is error recovery - JSON.parse throws one error and stops. Building something that keeps trying, finds multiple issues, and explains them in plain English took most of the time. The auto-fix logic is essentially a series of educated guesses applied in order, each one checked against JSON.parse until something passes. Ugly but effective. The other thing: people paste enormous JSON. Files that would choke a server-side tool work fine because the browser has plenty of memory and no upload limit. It's free, forever No ads on the tool pages. No signup. It runs on goodwill - there's a support button if you find it useful, but no pressure. If you work with JSON daily, give it a try. And if you build something similar, the client-side approach is worth considering.

entry.title: I Built a Universal CLI Scaffolding Tool — Scaffy v1.0.1 is Live
entry.summary:
I Built a Universal CLI Scaffolding Tool — Scaffy v1.0.1 is Live
Every time I started a new project, I found myself doing the same thing — So I built Scaffy. Scaffy is an open source CLI tool that scaffolds any framework in one command npm install -g scaffy-tool
scaffy laravel scaffy django scaffy next scaffy gin
You pick the framework, answer a few questions, and Scaffy handles the rest. Scaffy is built around a simple plugin system. Every framework is exactly plugin.json — metadata, requirements, version info questions.js — what to ask the user scaffold.js — what to run That's it. Anyone can add a new framework in 3 files and open a PR. After 3 sprints of development, v1.0.1 ships with 10 frameworks across
Language Frameworks
PHP Laravel v13, v12, v11 · Symfony v7
Python Django v5 · FastAPI
Go Gin v1
JavaScript ExpressJS v4 · NextJS v14 · NestJS v11 · VueJS v3
It uses official installers. Scaffy never ships its own templates. scaffy laravel runs composer create-project laravel/laravel. scaffy next runs npx create-next-app@14. You always get the freshest, It checks requirements first. Before running anything, Scaffy checks It detects your package manager. For JavaScript frameworks, Scaffy Node.js 18+ with full ESM Commander.js for CLI parsing Inquirer.js for interactive prompts Jest for testing (150+ tests) GitHub Actions CI on Node 18, 20, 22 scaffy add github:user/plugin — install community plugins AI mode — describe what you want, Scaffy picks the framework VS Code extension Plugin marketplace npm install -g scaffy-tool scaffy list
GitHub: https://github.com/TanvirHossen112/scaffy https://www.npmjs.com/package/scaffy-tool Would love feedback, issues, and PRs. If you want to add a framework, the plugin system makes it straightforward — open an issue and let's build it together.

entry.title: Why AI Agents Fail Silently — And How to Fix It
entry.summary: I spent three hours debugging an agent pipeline last week that wasn't broken. No errors. No exceptions. The logs looked fine. The agent ran, did its thing, and returned a response. The response just happened to be completely wrong. Nothing in my stack told me that. That's the problem. And if you're building anything with LLMs right now, you've almost certainly hit it already. The failure mode nobody talks about When a traditional API call breaks, you know. You get a 500, a timeout, an exception. Your monitoring catches it. Your retry logic kicks in. The system is designed around the assumption that failures are loud. LLMs don't work that way. An LLM can receive your prompt, process it fully, and return a confident, well-formatted, completely hallucinated response. No error code. No signal …

GHSA-H8R8-WCCR-V5F2: GHSA-H8R8-WCCR-V5F2: Mutation-XSS via Re-Contextualization in DOMPurify
entry.summary:
GHSA-H8R8-WCCR-V5F2: Mutation-XSS via Re-Contextualization in DOMPurify
Vulnerability ID: GHSA-H8R8-WCCR-V5F2 CVSS Score: 6.5 Published: 2026-03-27 DOMPurify versions prior to 3.3.2 are susceptible to a Mutation Cross-Site Scripting (mXSS) vulnerability. The flaw occurs due to discrepancies in browser parsing contexts when handling specific raw-text or RCDATA elements, allowing attackers to bypass sanitization. DOMPurify < 3.3.2 fails to properly neutralize specific raw-text elements like <noscript>. Attackers can inject payloads that bypass initial sanitization but mutate into executable JavaScript when re-inserted into the DOM. Vulnerability Type: Mutation Cross-Site Scripting (mXSS) CWE ID: CWE-79 CVSS v3.1 Score: 6.5 Medium Attack Vector: Network User Interaction: None Exploit Status: Proof of Concept Available Affected Component: Raw Text/RCDATA Parser Constraints DOMPurify (NPM Package) Client-side web applications utilizing DOMPurify < 3.3.2 dompurify: < 3.3.2 (Fixed in: 3.3.2) Advisory PoC: Proof of concept demonstrating <noscript> mutation via innerHTML assignment. Upgrade DOMPurify to version 3.3.2 or higher Implement strict Content Security Policy (CSP) rules restricting unsafe-inline scripts Avoid re-parsing sanitized content in differing browser contexts Audit dependency trees for transitive inclusions of vulnerable DOMPurify builds Remediation Steps: Identify all projects utilizing the DOMPurify NPM package. Execute dependency updates to force installation of DOMPurify >= 3.3.2. Validate the fix by executing test suites against known mXSS payloads. Deploy the updated application builds to production environments.
